description.narrative: Rationale <(>&<)> Objective: LaoCYDA’s project aims to fill these gaps by empowering youth leadership, fostering village–private sector collaboration, and embedding long-term CSA ownership in communities. The project will link youth and smallholder farmers with agribusinesses, social enterprises, and innovation hubs—enabling knowledge exchange, market access, and adoption of climate-resilienttechnologies. Key Activities <(>&<)> Expected Results: 1. Capacity Building with Youth and Private Sector Partners (Months1–2): LaoCYDA will train 40 youth mentors and 90 village youth volunteers, alongside 20 representatives from local private sector partners, including Phongsavanh Smart Agriculture Company and youth-led enterprises. Training will focus on CSA techniques, sustainable value chains, and market-driven climate solutions. 2. Village CSA Campaigns (Months 1–8): Youth leaders will deliver CSA outreach in all 15villages through storytelling, visual media, and role-play theatre, reaching approximately 1,500 people. Private sector partners will contribute demonstrations of CSA technologies, climate-resilient seeds, and eco-friendly inputs. 3. Community-Based Organizations(Months 6–12): Two pilot villages will form CBOs to manage CSA activities and coordinate withagribusiness buyers, enabling ongoing access to markets and resources beyond the project period. 4. District Dialogues <(>&<)> Policy Advocacy (Months 9–11): Youth–private sector coalitions will lead at least four district-level policy dialogues with PAFO, DAFO, MONRE, and MAF officials, and produce two CSA policy briefs highlighting youth-driven and market-linked solutions. 5. CSA Youth <(>&<)> Private Sector Toolkit (Month 12): A final CSA toolkit will compile campaign materials, youth stories, and policy insights to promote replication and learning. Target Groups <(>&<)> Reach: • 40 trained youth mentors and 90 village youth volunteers in 15 target villages • 20 private sector and social enterprise representatives from Luang Prabang <(>&<)> Savannakhet • ~1,500 villagers engaged directly through CSA events and demonstrations • Two CBOs established for ongoing CSA leadership and market linkages Impact: • Strengthened youth-led CSA action with strong private sector engagement • Enhanced adoption of climate-resilientfarming through technology and market access • Empowered communities with sustainable income and environmental resilience • Practical resources for replication via the CSA Youth <(>&<)> Private Sector Toolkit

LaoCYDA was officially approved by the Ministry of Home Affairs and all relevant government ministries on January 6, 2025. This date is recognized as the organization’s effective legal registration for programme management purposes. Counting from January6 throughAugust 4, 2025, LaoCYDA has approximately 0.6 years (about 7 months) of formal project management experience. The Founder <(>&<)> Director contributes more than 16 years of senior leadership experience in technical and management roles within international NGOs in Laos, including over three years as Country Director for ChildFund Australia in Laos (2022–2025). This proven leadership background support LaoCYDA’s institutional capabilities and programme management profile. Lao Child <(>&<)> Youth DevelopmentAssociation (LaoCYDA), officially registered by the Ministry of Home Affairs of Lao PDR on 6 January 2025, is a nationally mandated, locally led civil society organisation committed to the inclusive development of Lao children and youth. It partners withkey government ministries and national mass organizations. • Vision: “Lao Child and Youth Development Association (LaoCYDA) envisions to promote children’s rights, develop all children and youth in Laos reach their full potential in an inclusive society, regardless of gender, ethnicity, disability, and socio-economic background.” • Mission: “To empower the holistic development of Lao children and youth by ensuring their access to quality education, healthcare, and economic opportunities. We foster leadership, digital literacy, and environmental stewardship while promoting child and youth participation, advocacy, and youth-led initiatives through strategic partnerships with government, communities, and development partners.” LaoCYDA works across all provinces to cultivate youth leadership, deliver life-skills education, promote climate-resilient agriculture, and nurture entrepreneurship. Collaboration with ministries (Education <(>&<)> Sports; Health; Labour <(>&<)> Social Welfare; Agriculture <(>&<)> Forestry; NaturalResources <(>&<)> Environment), Lao Youth Union, and Lao Women’s Union ensures alignment with national strategies and Sustainable Development Goals.
